text: {"score":4,"justification":"The summary is accurate and grounded, with cautious language and specific numbers. Figures match the card: 19.2% vs 3.0% expected, risk-adjusted score 13.35, z 2.86, 34% low-complexity 99215s, 17 documented claims, 1 of 12 with no lab line. It is honest that documentation is too thin to conclude and that the leaning is inconclusive. The example claims cited fit their sentences: C0195484 (J06.9), C0196828 (J06.9), C0196127 (R21) and C0196139 (Z09) are all low-complexity 99215s, and C0196494 and C0196541 are high-complexity. The weaknesses are a few description mismatches, an internally tense framing, and next steps that are generic and do not match the narrative's own recommendation.","problems":["The narrative says to request charts for the specific low-complexity 99215s cited, but the coded next_steps only say to request a larger sample of 99214/99215 claims and re-screen; the next steps are generic and not tied to specific claim IDs.","The sampled diagnoses are described as 'upper respiratory infection, UTI, rash or follow-up exam', but the card shows R21 (rash) and Z09 (follow-up exam) among the diagnoses, so the description is approximately right; however, the claim that these 'rarely warrant high-complexity MDM' is the summary's own inference, not from the packet.","The headline says 'in every complexity stratum' while also saying documentation is inconclusive. The leaning is 'inconclusive' but the rationale says 'leans toward concern', which is mixed messaging.","The comparison '14% for comparison providers' is a rate from a single documented 99215, so the comparison is statistically meaningless; this is only partly flagged.","The 0-condition stratum has a 7.1% share, versus 1.8% overall; the headline stresses 'well above expectation' without noting that some strata are modest in absolute terms."]}
